items.expected: Both molecule records provide validation evidence or a truthful bounded failure.

items.statement: The same explicitly defined MEP/electrostatic-potential descriptor and atom-resolved charge convention are used to compare the two molecules and the four mapped alkene carbons; the public task permits any defensible charge partition when its definition and scope are explicit.
items.expected: The submission provides both a consistently defined MEP/electrostatic-potential result and atom-indexed, method-linked charge comparisons rather than an unsupported visual claim.

items.statement: The source comparison is consistent with asymmetric C=C density in 4 and comparatively symmetric C=C density in 7.
items.expected: The independent result distinguishes the two cases with signed alkene-carbon evidence.

items.statement: Any proposed explanation remains a reactant-state electronic rationale and does not claim that charges alone prove a unique haloetherification mechanism.
items.expected: The final interpretation states the causal and conformational limits.

items.statement: The two specified reactant models are compared in the stated aqueous boundary using a consistently defined MEP/electrostatic-potential descriptor and one explicitly defined atom-resolved charge convention at the four mapped alkene carbon sites, establishing the electronic polarization contrast without making a method-specific charge model mandatory.

rules.expected: Both molecule validation records are present and scientifically defensible, or bounded failure is honestly documented.
A common descriptor/charge definition and explicit atom-indexed alkene assignments support the comparison.
The independent result distinguishes the asymmetric 4 case from the comparatively symmetric 7 case with signed alkene evidence.
The comparison uses calculated atom-resolved reactant charges to evaluate the defined electronic polarization contrast.

The two specified reactant models are compared within the defined aqueous boundary using both (1) a consistently defined MEP/electrostatic-potential descriptor and (2) a clearly stated, scientifically appropriate atom-resolved charge convention at the four mapped alkene carbon sites. MK is an admissible charge partition, not a mandatory one; omitting either requested observable is incomplete.

items.condition: Atom order, alkene-carbon identity, charge state, or multiplicity is missing or inconsistent, preventing a fair comparison of the public molecules.
The submission gives no testable hypothesis or explanation linking its descriptor to the observed electronic contrast.
The submission overclaims that reactant-state charges alone establish a unique reaction mechanism.
